- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3–4% above prior peak.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-period, model lags in catching the reversal; adjust forecast to align with sentiment shift.
- Mean reversion is evident when model holds price near recent high/low; if sentiment is neutral or weak, reduce bias toward extremes.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; smooth out extremes with 5–7 day moving average of sentiment-weighted price.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “+0.33” or “+0.67” patterns, model tends to overcorrect; apply dampening factor of 0.85 to forecast if sentiment is trending upward.
